Way down in Florida's Treasure coast, a long long ago in the age of alternative music, there was a thing called the buzz bake fest. It was an annual collection of bands from the era of alternative rock. One year they had all this hubub hard rock shit going on - Powerman 5000, Union Underground and whatnot - but the biggest crowd reaction and moshpit came from the Mighty Mighty Bosstones on the dinky little side stage. People from across the Amphitheater came running to see why everyone else was running in that direction, until a pile of bodies in what I can only describe as a gravemind zombie horde straight out of the movies was surging on the side stage area. The people went crazy and some errant, angular motion slowly started coalescing deep in the center of the crowd until a giant circle pit broke out. Under the direction of the Mighty Mighty Bosstones, the Pre-hipsters, post-gothics, grunge hold-outs, and shirtless 40 somethings resembling tank abott all came together to produce the best energy of the entire day - and it was only 3 or 4pm. Swirling madness as the chunks of crowd would finally build up the courage to jump in the circle pit and be swept away in entrance and exit motions not dissimilar from the UK roundabout - jumping in here, jumping out there because you're not sure when the next time you'll be able to escape the circle pit - guys and girls linking arms and being thrown into the system like Conway's game of life, only to be broken down into smaller chunks of linked chains while colliding and bouncing off of sweaty bodies.

Whoever was running the fest asked the Mighty Mighty Bosstones to fill in for bands that didn't show up, and they went on to play 2 more sets later that day and night!

Good shit. And this is coming from a guy who has seen numerous metalcore/hardcore pits and all the violence and freak shows they bring. The positive energy and level of fun during the Mighty Mighty Bosstones was massive.
